Speed it up into a ten-second clip with dramatic music.
missions.finish: Your makeover film is ten seconds of glory.
missions.apart: Each make a film of your own makeover and premiere them for each other.

missions.title: Pack each other's lunch
missions.supplies: Lunch ingredients, containers, a scrap of paper
missions.description: Make tomorrow's lunch for each other, with one surprise and a little note tucked inside.
steps: Each make a lunch for the other using what's in the kitchen.
Add one surprise: a favorite snack, a fun shape, a little treat.
Tuck in a note for them to find.
Report back after lunch tomorrow.
missions.finish: Both lunches have been eaten and reviewed.
missions.apart: Send a photo of the lunch you'd pack for them; they make it and eat it with your note read aloud on a call.

missions.title: Junior explorer badge
missions.supplies: A phone camera, paper and pens for the badge
missions.description: Earn a homemade explorer badge by finding something fuzzy, spotted, perfectly round and very tiny outside.
steps: Head out for a walk with your list: fuzzy, spotted, round, tiny.
Photograph each find without picking anything up.
Once you've got all four, draw each other an explorer badge.
Award them with a solemn ceremony.
missions.finish: Both badges have been awarded.
missions.apart: Each find the four things where you are and send photos; award badges on video.

missions.title: Audio mystery in the dark
missions.supplies: A speaker and a free audio drama or mystery podcast
missions.description: Turn off the lights, play a free audio mystery, and try to solve it before the reveal.
steps: Find a free audio mystery or short radio play.
Turn the lights down and get under a blanket.
Pause it before the final reveal.
Each name your suspect and your reason, then hit play.
missions.finish: The mystery is solved and you know who guessed right.
missions.apart: Press play at the same time on a call and pause together before the reveal.

missions.title: Greenhouse jungle visit
missions.supplies: Check opening times and any small entry fee
missions.description: Visit a public greenhouse or botanical garden glasshouse and hunt for the strangest plant inside.
steps: Find a public greenhouse, conservatory or botanical garden near you.
Wander slowly through the warm, damp air.
Each find the strangest plant and read its label.
Take a photo of the two of you in the most jungle-like corner.
missions.finish: You've each found a strange plant and have a jungle photo.
missions.apart: Each visit a greenhouse or plant shop near you, or take a free virtual tour of a famous glasshouse.

missions.title: Walk-on music
missions.description: Pick dramatic walk-on songs for each other and make grand entrances into the room.
steps: Each secretly pick a walk-on song for the other.
One of you steps outside the room.
Hit play and they make a full entrance: waving, posing, whatever the song demands.
Swap, then decide whose song choice was perfect.
missions.finish: You've both made an entrance to your song.
missions.apart: Play their song on your end and they make an entrance into their camera's frame.

missions.title: Sock basketball court
missions.supplies: A paper cup or small box, tape, rolled-up socks
missions.description: Build a mini basketball hoop from a cup or box and shoot rolled-up socks for points.
steps: Cut the bottom out of a paper cup or use a small open box as a hoop.
Tape it to a door or the back of a chair.
Mark three shooting lines worth 1, 2 and 3 points.
Play to 21.
missions.finish: Someone has reached 21 points.
missions.apart: Each build a hoop and play over video, calling your own scores honestly.

missions.title: Virtual garden stroll
missions.description: Wander through a famous garden on a free virtual tour and pick the corner you'd sit in for an afternoon.
steps: Find a free virtual tour or Street View walk through a famous garden.
Wander slowly and take turns choosing the direction.
Each screenshot the spot you'd want to sit in.
Explain why yours is the best bench.
missions.finish: You've both chosen your perfect garden spot.
missions.apart: Share your screen on a call and take turns steering.

missions.title: Three-item costume department
missions.description: Create a whole character from just three things grabbed from around the house in sixty seconds.
steps: Set a sixty-second timer.
Each grab three things: a scarf, a spoon, a lampshade.
Put them on and become a character with a name and a catchphrase.
Introduce yourselves to each other in character.
missions.finish: Both characters have made their debut.
missions.apart: Run the timer on a call and reveal your characters on camera.

missions.title: Neighborhood awards night
missions.description: Hand out tiny awards to ordinary neighborhood things, like Best Garden Gnome and Most Dramatic Tree.
steps: Make up five award categories before you leave.
Walk around and nominate contenders as you go.
Photograph the winners.
Give acceptance speeches on their behalf on the way home.
missions.finish: All five awards have winners and speeches.
missions.apart: Each run the awards in your neighborhood and compare winners on a call.

missions.title: Tiny world for a toy
missions.supplies: A small toy or figurine, household objects
missions.description: Turn everyday objects into a miniature landscape for a small toy, then photograph it at toy level.
steps: Pick a small toy as your hero.
Build its world: a broccoli forest, a mirror lake, a book mountain.
Get your phone down to the toy's eye level.
Take three photos that tell a little adventure.
missions.finish: Your toy has a world and a three-photo adventure.
missions.apart: Each build a world and send photos; make the toys 'visit' each other.

missions.title: Battleship on paper
missions.description: Play Battleship with nothing but two sheets of graph paper and a lot of suspense.
steps: Each draw two 10-by-10 grids labeled A to J and 1 to 10.
Secretly place five ships of different lengths on one grid.
Take turns calling squares like 'B7' and mark hits and misses.
First to sink all five ships wins.
missions.finish: Someone's fleet has been sunk.
missions.apart: Play over a call or text; it works beautifully at any distance.

missions.title: Sheet-pan supper
missions.supplies: Vegetables, a protein of your choice, oil, seasoning, a baking tray
missions.description: Chop together, throw everything on one tray, and let the oven do the rest while you take a break.
steps: Each pick two vegetables and one seasoning.
Chop everything into similar-sized pieces.
Toss with oil and seasoning and spread on one tray.
Roast at 425°F (220°C) for about 30 minutes, checking that everything's cooked through.
missions.finish: Supper's out of the oven and on your plates.
missions.apart: Make your own trays on a call and eat together on video.

missions.title: Font detectives
missions.description: Study the lettering on three nearby signs and figure out what each font is trying to say about itself.
steps: Walk past shops and signs and photograph three very different letter styles.
Describe each one's personality: fancy, friendly, bossy.
Look up one to learn its name.
Decide which font you'd each use on your front door.
missions.finish: Three signs studied and one font identified.
missions.apart: Each find three signs and trade photos.

missions.title: Wrap a gift with no tape
missions.supplies: A square scarf or piece of fabric, a small gift
missions.description: Wrap something for someone using a scarf or square of fabric, Japanese furoshiki style.
steps: Look up a simple furoshiki wrapping method.
Choose a small gift for someone: a book, a jar of cookies, a plant.
Practice the fold on each other first.
Wrap it and give it away; the fabric is part of the gift.
missions.finish: Your gift is wrapped and given.
missions.apart: Each wrap a gift on a call and mail them to each other.

missions.title: Recipe for a perfect moment
missions.description: Write a recipe card for recreating one small, perfect moment you shared.
steps: Pick a small, good moment: a rainy afternoon, a long walk, a silly dinner.
Write it as a recipe: ingredients, method, serving suggestion.
Add a 'chef's note' about why it worked.
Keep the card in a recipe box or drawer.
missions.finish: Your recipe card is written and filed.
missions.apart: Write one each, mail them or read them aloud on a call.

missions.title: Puzzle postcard
missions.supplies: A postcard or card, a stamp
missions.description: Send your partner a postcard with a tiny puzzle hidden on it, like a riddle, a code or a dot-to-dot.
steps: Pick a puzzle type: a riddle, a simple code, a maze.
Hide it on a postcard with a picture or note.
Mail it.
Your partner sends a photo of the solution when it arrives.
missions.finish: The postcard has arrived and been solved.
missions.apart: Made for distance: snail mail makes the wait part of the fun.

missions.title: Speed sketch the street
missions.description: Sketch the same street scene three times: in two minutes, then thirty seconds, then ten.
steps: Find a street scene to sketch.
Draw it in two minutes.
Draw it again in thirty seconds, then in ten.
Compare and decide which version has the most charm.
missions.finish: You've each drawn three versions.
missions.apart: Each sketch your own street and swap photos.

missions.title: Bounce the light
missions.supplies: A phone, white paper or foil, a window
missions.description: Use a sheet of white paper or foil to make a portrait or object photo look like it was shot in a studio.
steps: Sit by a window and take a plain photo.
Hold white paper or foil on the shady side to bounce light back.
Take the same photo again.
Compare and swap roles.
missions.finish: You've each taken a before-and-after photo.
missions.apart: Bounce your own light and send before-and-after selfies.

missions.title: Fairy tale, wrong genre
missions.supplies: Paper slips and a bowl; a phone if you want to film
missions.description: Retell a famous fairy tale as a heist movie, a nature documentary or a cooking competition.
steps: Write five genres on slips: heist, horror, sports broadcast, cooking show, nature documentary.
Pick a fairy tale you both know, then draw a genre.
Act out the whole story in under five minutes, fully committed to the genre.
Draw a new genre and do it again with roles swapped.
missions.finish: You've performed the tale in two different genres.
missions.apart: Text each other the genre you drew and perform for each other on video.

missions.title: Pantry roulette
missions.description: Each pick three random things from the pantry for the other, then cook something tasty that uses all three.
steps: Each choose three ingredients for your partner; be fair, not cruel.
Take five minutes to plan a snack or small dish around them.
Cook side by side, borrowing basics like oil, salt and eggs as needed.
Taste both and award points for flavor and creativity.
missions.finish: Both dishes are cooked, tasted and scored.
missions.apart: Pick from your own pantries over a call, show each other your three, and cook on video.

missions.title: Nature documentary narrator
missions.description: Film a pigeon, a squirrel or a very still houseplant and narrate it like a world-famous wildlife show.
steps: Find your subject: a bird, a bug, a neighbor's cat, a plant.
Film thirty seconds from a respectful distance.
Record a hushed, dramatic narration over it, sticking to what really happens.
Watch both films and nominate one for an award.
missions.finish: Two wildlife films are narrated and one has been nominated.
missions.apart: Each film your own wildlife and narrate each other's clip.

missions.title: Word ladder over tea
missions.supplies: Paper and a pen, a warm drink
missions.description: Turn one word into another by changing one letter at a time, working together with a pot of tea.
steps: Pick a start and end word with the same number of letters, like CAT to DOG.
Take turns changing one letter so each step is a real word (CAT, COT, DOT, DOG).
If you're stuck, you can go back a step and try another route.
Once you've finished, try a harder pair, like WARM to COLD.
missions.finish: You've finished at least two ladders.
missions.apart: Play on a call, writing your steps on paper and reading them out.

missions.title: Free thing we've never tried
missions.description: Find a free local event you'd normally scroll past, like a library talk or a community class, and just go.
steps: Check a library board, community center or local events page for something free this week.
Each pick one option, then flip a coin.
Go with open minds and stay for the whole thing.
On the way home, each share one thing you learned or liked.
missions.finish: You've been and each shared one takeaway.
missions.apart: Each find a free event near you, or join the same free online class or talk together.

missions.title: Cover song showdown
missions.description: Each find the best cover version of a song your partner loves, then play it against the original.
steps: Each name a song you love.
Hunt for a cover of your partner's song: a different genre, a choir, a ukulele version.
Play the original, then the cover.
Your partner decides whether the cover wins.
missions.finish: Both covers have been played and judged.
missions.apart: Send each other the cover link and listen together on a call.

missions.title: Spoon catapult contest
missions.supplies: Spoons, rubber bands, a small block or stack of erasers, paper balls
missions.description: Build a catapult from a spoon, rubber bands and a block, then see whose launches a paper ball furthest.
steps: Rubber-band a spoon to the top of a small block or stack so the bowl sticks out.
Load a small paper ball into the spoon.
Press down and let go, aiming away from faces and breakables.
Measure each launch and tweak your design for three rounds.
missions.finish: Three rounds launched and a distance champion named.
missions.apart: Build on a video call and measure your launches on camera.

missions.title: Time-travel the internet
missions.description: Use the free Wayback Machine to see your favorite websites as they looked the year you met, or the year you turned ten.
steps: Open the Internet Archive's Wayback Machine.
Each pick a site you use a lot and a year that matters to you.
Look at the old version and find the most dated detail: tiny buttons, wild fonts, a forgotten logo.
Show each other and guess what else was happening in your lives that year.
missions.finish: You've both visited a website from the past and shared your favorite relic.
missions.apart: Share your screen on a call and take turns being tour guide.

missions.title: Other-hand hour
missions.description: For one hour, do everything with your non-dominant hand: eat, write, brush, scroll. It gets hilarious fast.
steps: Agree on a start time and switch hands.
Do ordinary things: make a snack, write your names, text each other.
Keep score of slip-ups; using your usual hand costs a point.
End by comparing your best other-hand signature.
missions.finish: The hour is over and both signatures have been compared.
missions.apart: Do it at the same time in your own homes and send each other other-hand messages.

missions.title: Five-minute paper city
missions.description: Draw a city together in five minutes, taking turns adding one building, street or tiny drama at a time.
steps: Set a timer for five minutes.
Take turns adding one thing: a skyscraper, a park, a runaway hot-air balloon.
No erasing; build around any mistakes.
Name the city when the timer ends.
missions.finish: Your city is drawn and named.
missions.apart: Draw on a shared online whiteboard or each draw half and combine the photos.

missions.title: Map it from memory
missions.description: Draw a map of a short walk you do all the time, then walk it to see what you forgot.
steps: Pick a route you both know well, like the walk to a cafe or a park.
Each draw it from memory with every landmark you can remember.
Walk the route together, map in hand.
Count what you missed and what you made up.
missions.finish: You've walked the route and checked both maps.
missions.apart: Each draw a route from your own neighborhood, walk it, and share your corrections.

missions.title: Potato stamp studio
missions.supplies: A potato, a small knife, paint or ink, paper
missions.description: Carve simple shapes into halved potatoes and print your own patterned cards or paper.
steps: Cut a potato in half and pat the cut sides dry.
Carefully carve a simple raised shape into each: a heart, a star, a leaf.
Dab on paint and stamp onto paper.
Make a card for someone using both stamps.
missions.finish: You've printed a card with both of your stamps.
missions.apart: Each carve a stamp on a call and mail each other something printed with it.

missions.title: Spoon delivery service
missions.supplies: Spoons, a small folded paper parcel, cushions and chairs for obstacles
missions.description: Carry a paper parcel on a spoon through a living-room obstacle course without dropping it.
steps: Build a short course: round the chair, under the table, over a cushion.
Fold a small paper 'parcel' and balance it on a spoon.
Take turns delivering it, timed; a drop means back to the start.
Add a new obstacle for each round.
missions.finish: Three deliveries each, and the fastest courier crowned.
missions.apart: Build courses at home and time each other over video.

missions.title: Mystery snack swap
missions.description: Each pick one snack you've never tried from a local shop and taste them together.
steps: Visit a local shop, ideally one with snacks you don't know.
Each secretly choose one mystery snack for the other.
Open them at home together.
Rate them for taste and surprise.
missions.finish: Both snacks are tasted and rated.
missions.apart: Each buy one locally and taste them together on a call, describing the flavor.

missions.title: Lift a book with one finger
missions.supplies: A ruler, a pencil, a book
missions.description: Use a ruler and a pencil as a lever and discover how moving the pivot changes everything.
steps: Lay the pencil on a table and balance the ruler across it.
Put a book on one end of the ruler.
Press the other end with one finger, moving the pencil closer to or further from the book.
Find where it's easiest and explain why to each other.
missions.finish: You've found the easiest pivot point and explained it.
missions.apart: Try it on a call with your own books and compare results.

missions.title: Water a thirsty street tree
missions.supplies: A watering can or a couple of big bottles of water
missions.description: On a dry, hot week, give a young street or park tree near you a long drink.
steps: Look for a young tree near you, with a thin trunk, that looks dry.
Check that it's okay to water it; most young street trees are glad of help.
Pour a couple of big cans slowly around the base so it soaks in.
Come back a few days later to say hello and water it again.
missions.finish: Your tree has had at least two drinks this week.
missions.apart: Each adopt a thirsty tree where you live and send a photo after every watering.

missions.title: Save your first try
missions.description: Both try something you've never done, like a self-portrait or a haiku, and save it as a dated first attempt.
steps: Pick something neither of you has really tried: a haiku, a self-portrait, a comic panel.
Each give it one honest attempt in ten minutes.
Write the date and one line on how it felt on the back.
Tuck both into a folder marked 'First tries' to look back on once you've had more practice.
missions.finish: Both first tries are dated and filed away.
missions.apart: Make your attempts on a call and mail them to each other to keep.

missions.title: Two-screen movie premiere
missions.supplies: A free short film online, snacks, something fancy to wear
missions.description: Pick a free short film and hold a red-carpet premiere from your two homes, with outfits, snacks and reviews.
steps: Choose a free short film, under 20 minutes, from a site that streams shorts legally.
Dress up a little and do a red-carpet photo on camera.
Count down and press play at the same moment.
Afterward, each give it a star rating and a one-line critic's quote.
missions.finish: The film is watched and both reviews are in.
missions.apart: Made for distance: a quick 'three, two, one' keeps you in sync.

missions.title: Twenty-word art review
missions.description: Review one piece of public art in exactly twenty words. Not nineteen, not twenty-one.
steps: Find a mural, sculpture, mosaic or even a striking bit of graffiti.
Look at it quietly for two full minutes.
Each write a review of exactly twenty words.
Read them aloud and give the art a star rating together.
missions.finish: Both twenty-word reviews are written and read.
missions.apart: Each review a piece near you and send a photo with your review.

missions.title: Photo clue treasure hunt
missions.supplies: A phone, a small treat or note
missions.description: Hide a small treat, then lead your partner to it with a trail of close-up photo clues.
steps: One of you hides a small treat or note somewhere at home.
Take four close-up photos of spots along the way, each one hiding the next clue.
Show the first photo; your partner finds that spot and gets the next photo.
Swap roles for a second hunt.
missions.finish: Both treasures have been found.
missions.apart: Hide something in your own home and send photo clues; your partner guides you to it by guessing each spot.

missions.title: One-take hallway epic
missions.supplies: A phone and a few props
missions.description: Film a whole adventure in one continuous shot that moves through your home, with no cuts allowed.
steps: Plan a tiny plot that moves from room to room: a chase, a quest, a lost sock.
One of you holds the camera, the other is the star.
Rehearse the route once, then film it in a single take with no stopping.
If something goes wrong, keep going; mistakes become plot twists.
missions.finish: You've filmed one complete take from start to finish.
missions.apart: Each film a one-take adventure through your own home and premiere them on a call.

missions.title: One dough, two cookies
missions.supplies: Basic cookie ingredients, two mix-ins (chocolate, raisins, spices)
missions.description: Make one batch of cookie dough, split it in half, and each choose a different mix-in.
steps: Make a simple cookie dough together.
Split it into two bowls.
Each add a different mix-in or spice.
Bake, taste and decide which deserves the whole batch next time.
missions.finish: Both versions are baked and a winner chosen.
missions.apart: Bake on a call, each picking a different mix-in, and swap tasting notes.

missions.title: Ten-minute bird tally
missions.supplies: Paper and pen, a free bird ID app if you like
missions.description: Sit by a window or in a park for ten minutes and count every bird you see.
steps: Find a window or bench with a bit of sky or trees.
Set a ten-minute timer.
Tally every bird, describing any you don't know.
Look up one new bird afterward.
missions.finish: Your ten-minute tally is done and one bird identified.
missions.apart: Each do your own tally and compare which birds you share.

missions.title: Show-and-tell for grown-ups
missions.description: Show each other one small thing you love about a hobby or interest the other doesn't know much about.
steps: Each pick one small thing: a stitch, a game move, a favorite book passage, a chord.
Take five minutes to show it, explaining why you love it.
Your partner asks one curious question and tries it themselves.
Swap, then pick one thing you'd like to learn more about.
missions.finish: Both show-and-tells are done.
missions.apart: Do it on video, holding things up to the camera.

missions.title: Departure-board daydreams
missions.description: Sit in a train or bus station, read the departure board, and plan which trip you'd take if you could leave right now.
steps: Find a seat with a view of a departure board at a station.
Each pick the destination you'd hop on to, right now, no packing.
Plan your first hour there: what you'd eat, where you'd walk.
Before you leave, choose one you'd actually like to visit someday.
missions.finish: You've each chosen a dream departure and planned your first hour.
missions.apart: Pull up the live departures for a station in each of your cities and plan imaginary trips on a call.

missions.title: Happy Birthday in five styles
missions.description: Sing 'Happy Birthday' as an opera, a lullaby, a country ballad, a rock anthem and a whisper.
steps: Write five styles on slips of paper.
Take turns drawing a slip and singing in that style.
Commit fully; half-hearted opera doesn't count.
Vote for the version that deserves a real birthday.
missions.finish: All five styles have been performed.
missions.apart: Sing on a call and save the best version for each other's real birthday.

missions.title: No-tape phone stand
missions.description: Build a sturdy phone stand from a single piece of cardboard using only folds and slots.
steps: Sketch a design that folds into a triangle or a slotted easel.
Cut and fold the cardboard.
Test it by watching a short video.
Improve the weakest point and test again.
missions.finish: Your stand holds a phone steady through a whole video.
missions.apart: Build on a video call and use your stands for the rest of the call.

missions.title: Pixel room designers
missions.description: Design a tiny dream room on an 8-by-8 pixel grid using a free online pixel art tool.
steps: Open a free pixel art site and set the canvas to 8 by 8.
Each design a tiny room: a bed, a window, a plant.
Show each other and guess what each pixel is.
Combine them into a two-room pixel house.
missions.finish: Both rooms are designed and combined.
missions.apart: Share screens on a call to combine your rooms.

missions.title: Sketch picnic
missions.description: Take a simple picnic outside and spend half of it sketching the same view in your own styles.
steps: Pack a simple picnic and two sketchbooks or sheets of paper.
Find a spot with a view.
Eat, then sketch for twenty minutes without peeking at each other's.
Reveal your sketches at the same time.
missions.finish: Your picnic is eaten and both sketches are revealed.
missions.apart: Each picnic and sketch where you are and swap photos.
